Shared middle representations emerge as models grow and train on more data.

quiz.q: Why do larger models share one concept space across languages?

Word prediction works because the dictionary of words is finite.

quiz.q: Why does next-token prediction handle text but fail on video?

quiz.q: Why does imitating human behavior not build a world model?

summary: The speaker explains self-attention builds query, key and value vectors per token, then mixes values by match scores. The same word gets a different output vector depending on context, so 'bank' reflects its neighbors.
points: Query is what a token looks for; key is what it offers.

Multiple heads run in parallel and specialize during training, not by design.

quiz.a: Query is what a token seeks and key what it offers; 'bank' near 'river' and 'muddy' gets a river-shaped vector from its neighbors' values.
quiz.q: How does context change the vector for the word 'bank'?

Predicting a word should use only the context before it.

quiz.a: Softmax zeroes future positions after minus infinity is added, so a decoder token attends only to earlier tokens and itself.
quiz.q: Why does minus infinity in the causal mask matter for decoder LLMs?

quiz.q: How do transformers let every word look at all others at once?

hook: Query, key and value in self-attention, intuitively
why: Clear intuition for tokens asking, answering and weighting each other.

subject: self-attention
summary: The speaker explains that each token derives query, key and value vectors from its embedding. A token's query is scored against other tokens' keys, and the match weights how much of their values it takes.
points: Attention weights show how much each token attends to others.
Query asks what a token needs; key offers what it represents.
Dot product of query and key gives a relevance score.

quiz.a: A query asks what a token needs, a key offers what it represents; their dot product gives a relevance score that weights values.
quiz.q: What do query and key vectors each contribute to self-attention?

hook: Why LLMs mask future tokens in attention

title: How Attention Mechanism Works in Transformer Architecture
subject: causal masking
summary: The speaker argues attention must be masked so each token cannot see future tokens, since language models predict the next token. A mask of negative infinity added to the scores becomes zero weight after softmax.

Adding negative infinity to future positions zeroes their attention after softmax.
The first token attends only to itself, giving it full weight.

quiz.a: Language models predict next tokens, so each token must not see future ones; adding negative infinity to future scores gives zero weight after softmax.
quiz.q: Why must attention mask future tokens during language model training?
